data.title: Seoul weighs steps to force North Korea landmine apology
data.description: SEOUL — South Korea is considering measures to force an apology from North Korea over a recent landmine blast that injured three soldiers inside the Demiltarised Zone (DMZ), its defence ministry said Tuesday.

data.title: Ready, set, snooze: Sleep-deprived Japanese compete for best-rested
data.description: TOKYO — In diligent, exhausted Japan, self-described elite "competitive sleepers" vied to lie down, relax and nap the fastest and deepest in a contest organised by a mattress company.

data.title: COP31 eyes modest steps as climate disasters multiply
data.description: PARIS - Nations reeling from a year of climate devastation gather for COP31 next month but negotiations are not expected to deliver major progress in cutting the fossil fuels driving the crisis.

data.title: Tens of thousands expected in Paris for high school protests
data.description: PARIS — Tens of thousands of demonstrators are expected on the streets of Paris on Tuesday as France's powerful trade unions join high school students rallying for better conditions in a wave of protests marked by clashes with police.

data.title: American Nobel laureate in medicine hopes to illuminate the brain
data.description: WASHINGTON - Nobel Prize-winning American researcher Karl Deisseroth is a psychiatrist, neuroscientist and bioengineer who has spent more than two decades illuminating the workings of the brain to unlock its mysteries.

data.title: Trump approves firing squad for convicted US military base shooter
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - President Donald Trump has approved the execution by firing squad of Nidal Hasan, a US Army psychiatrist who shot dead 13 people at a military base in 2009, the Pentagon said on Monday.

data.title: Grappling with 'homework scams,' US universities shun AI detectors
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - Locked in a cat-and-mouse struggle, biology professor Timothy Paustian devised novel ways to catch students turning in chatbot-generated assignments. But like many US universities, his institution is shunning AI detection software.

data.title: Russia downplays plague reports as Trump offers US help
data.description: MOSCOW - Russia on Monday sought to downplay reports that a laboratory technician had died of plague, even as President Donald Trump said Washington was closely monitoring the situation and offered US help.

data.title: Nigeria's Tinubu confirms 32 dead after military plane crash
data.description: LAGOS - A Nigerian Air Force plane crashed on Monday in the country's southwestern Ondo state, killing all 32 people on board, President Bola Tinubu said.

data.title: Switching on brain cells: the Nobel-winning science of optogenetics
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - In optogenetics, scientists control neurones by stimulating them with light -- potentially unlocking breakthroughs for conditions such as dementia, depression and blindness.

data.title: Clashes erupt outside Kosovo parliament over war crimes court
data.description: - Police clashed with demonstrators outside Kosovo's parliament on Monday, as protesters demanded the passage of a bill that would curb the powers of the country's war crimes court.

data.title: At Oct 7 memorial, Netanyahu says will be no Hamas rule in Gaza
data.description: JERUSALEM - Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Monday vowed there would be no Hamas rule in Gaza as he attended a memorial event marking three years since the militant group's October 7, 2023 attack.

data.title: UN rights council slams Taliban's 'oppression' of women
data.description: GENEVA - The United Nations' Human Rights Council on Monday unanimously urged the Taliban to repeal all practices restricting the fundamental freedoms of women and girls, saying Afghanistan's institutionalised discrimination should shock humanity.

data.title: Bolsonaro rides right-wing surge into Brazil's election runoff
data.description: BRASíLIA - Right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro heads to an October 25 runoff election from a position of strength, riding a conservative wave that has left President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva facing a tough battle to win a fourth term.

data.title: Ukraine says using AI robot guns to shoot down new Russian drones
data.description: KYIV — Ukraine has begun using artificial intelligence-enabled robot guns to take down Russia's new and fast-moving jet-powered drones, the Ukrainian air force said Monday.

data.title: Former Prince Andrew files legal action against UK police after arrest
data.description: LONDON — Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, formerly known as Prince Andrew, has begun legal action against the British police force that arrested him and searched his properties this year as part of its investigation into his links to Jeffrey Epstein.

data.title: Disgraced former US House speaker dies at 84
data.description: WASHINGTON — Dennis Hastert, the longest-serving Republican speaker of the US House of Representatives whose career ended in disgrace after he admitted sexually abusing teenage boys he had coached, has died aged 84, officials said Monday.

data.title: Spain's PM calls snap election after housing bill defeat
data.description: MADRID - Spain's prime minister on Monday called a snap election for November 29, after the country's parliament rejected housing relief measures proposed by his minority government amid nationwide protests.

data.title: Alleged Indian leader of neo-Nazi child abuse ring goes on trial in Paris
data.description: PARIS — An Indian man went on trial in Paris on Monday, accused of running a neo-Nazi child exploitation ring in which young girls were allegedly coerced into performing sexual acts online and engaging in self-harm.

data.title: Two dead, 11 rescued after fire onboard ship in Black Sea
data.description: BUCHAREST - Romanian authorities said on ​Monday that two people ‌had died and others had been rescued after a fire on a ship in the Black Sea outside Romania's territorial waters.

data.title: Slovenian glacier, tracked since 1946, could disappear within days
data.description: MOUNT ​TRIGLAV — Once a magnet for ​summer skiers and cherished by generations as a ​symbol of Slovenia's Alpine heritage, ‌one of the country's last glaciers has dwindled to a few patches of ice that researchers say could disappear within days.

data.title: Hundreds of French high schools shut as protests persist
data.description: PARIS — Lessons were suspended at hundreds of French high schools on Monday, as part of a wave of student protest over learning conditions that have rocked the European nation.

data.title: Spain PM calls early election after housing crisis defeat
data.description: MADRID - Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez on Monday called a snap election for November 29, after parliament rejected housing relief measures proposed by his minority government.

data.title: US arrests woman accused of spying for China on Taiwan leader's family
data.description: LOS ANGELES (UNITED STATES) - A woman accused of spying for China on Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te's son and his family in the United States was arrested Sunday, US and Taiwanese officials said.

data.title: Yemen military announces broad strikes against Houthis
data.description: TAIZ (YEMEN) - The Yemeni military announced a broad set of strikes against Houthi targets on Monday, after the government declared a new campaign to retake all territory even as the Iran-backed group made fresh gains on the ground.

data.title: Myanmar says 10,000 migrants returned from Malaysia this year
data.description: YANGON (MYANMAR) - Myanmar has repatriated nearly 10,000 migrants from Malaysia this year, state media said on Monday, a day after a flotilla returning almost 1,500 of its citizens docked in the country.

data.title: About 360 people tow Pokemon aircraft at Narita airport
data.description: About 360 children and adults joined forces to tow a roughly 133-tonne Boeing 787 aircraft decorated with Pokemon characters at Narita airport near Tokyo, moving it about 80 metres in an event to spur interest in aviation.

data.title: Three years on, Israeli rescuer cannot escape October 7
data.description: JERUSALEM - Israeli rescuer Natan Kenig says it does not take much of a trigger for him to relive the October 7, 2023 attack: his eyes open or closed, at home or out with friends, he still sees the rockets, torched cars and lifeless bodies.

data.title: EU, China to hold Beijing talks to avert trade war
data.description: BRUSSELS - EU trade chief Maros Sefcovic will head to Beijing on Thursday for two days of make-or-break meetings with Chinese officials to try to stave off a trade war.

data.title: Research into weight-loss drugs tipped for Nobel as award week opens
data.description: STOCKHOLM - Research into hormones that regulate appetite is on everybody's lips for the Nobel medicine prize, to be announced on Monday when the 2026 Nobel season kicks off.

data.title: Rubio visits Iceland as US boosts Arctic presence
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - US Secretary of State Marco Rubio will travel Monday to Iceland to continue pressing US interests in the Arctic, two weeks after Washington sealed a security pact on Greenland.
